commitResults.messageTitle: Unregister list cells' highlight listener via a weak reference
commitResults.messageBody:
Each PersonListViewCell added a listener to the panel-lifetime
recentlyAddedPerson property without removing it, so cells the ListView
discarded could not be garbage-collected, and every command notified
the accumulated dead listeners. Register it through a WeakChangeListener,
held in a cell field, so it is dropped once the cell is collected. The
highlight behaviour is unchanged, since updateItem still re-applies it.

Fixes #202

commitResults.messageTitle: Confirm clear with Y in the comprehensive input test
commitResults.messageBody:
ComprehensiveInputTest ran 'clear' but never sent the Y confirmation,
so the roster was never emptied. Every following 'empty roster' check
and the advanced sort checks then ran against a full roster and failed,
breaking the build on master. Send Y after each clear so the roster is
actually emptied, matching the clear-confirmation behaviour.

commitResults.messageTitle: Match phone searches consistently with the significant-digits key
commitResults.messageBody:
find p/ compared the raw phone text, so find p/91234567 did not match a
number stored as 9123 4567, even though duplicate detection and sorting
already treat those as the same number. Reduce the stored phone and the
p/ keyword through one Phone.significantDigitsOf helper (also used by
getSignificantDigits), so p/ find is consistent with duplicate detection
and sorting: formatting and bracketed notes are ignored, and a keyword
with no digits matches nothing. Broad find matches both those digits and
the phone's displayed text, so a number is findable by its real digits
(find 659 finds (+65) 9123 4567) or by a note (find HP).

Re-addresses #166.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject phones with two country codes or a note inside the number
commitResults.messageBody:
Phone validation accepted any mix of digit groups, country codes and
notes, so nonsense like (+65) (+65) 9123 or 9123 (HP) 4567 was saved.
Allow at most one country code, at the start, and only allow notes
before or after the number. Leading and trailing notes such as
(65) 9123-4567 and 9123 4567 (HP) still work.

Closes #213
Make phone find match the significant-digits key

commitResults.messageTitle: Treat a bracketed code before a phone number as part of it
commitResults.messageBody:
Bracketed digits were always stripped as a note, so (212) 123-4567 and
(555) 123-4567 collapsed to the same number, find p/212 found nothing,
and (65) 9123 4567 counted as a different number from (+65) 9123 4567.

Read bracketed text by position instead: a bracketed code before the
number, with or without a plus, contributes its digits, so (212) 1234
has the digits 2121234. Bracketed text after the number stays a note.
A leading bracket that is not just digits, such as (HP), is still an
ignored note. Saved rosters keep loading under the legacy grammar.

commitResults.messageTitle: Load lightly damaged data files and keep a pending clear after an empty Enter
commitResults.messageBody:
A saved roster with a blank age category, an address padded with spaces,
or no content at all was treated as wholly unreadable: the file was
renamed to a backup and TrackFlow started empty. These are all cases a
hand edit can produce, and none of them loses information, so load them
instead: a blank category becomes Open like a missing one, surrounding
whitespace around an address is removed, and an empty or whitespace-only
file is an empty roster.

The clear confirmation also dropped silently. Pressing Enter on an empty
command box while a clear was pending cancelled it with "No command
entered", so the Y that followed was reported as an unknown command.
An empty submission now shows the warning again and keeps the clear
pending, and typing Y or N when nothing is pending explains that a clear
must be started first.
Load lightly damaged data files and keep a pending clear after an empty Enter

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject on entry every duplicate the saved roster would reject on loading
commitResults.messageBody:
Adding an athlete with the same name and the same phone digits in a
different format, such as (9123) 4567 next to 9123 4567, passed the
command-side duplicate check (which compares Singapore-default keys)
but failed the stored-roster check (which compares significant digits).
The roster was saved before the stored check ran, so the command showed
an error while the file already held the pair, and the next launch
backed the file up and started with an empty roster.

Make the command-side rule a superset of the stored rule by also
matching phones on significant digits, and re-check the stored rule on
a copy of the staged roster before saving, so nothing that would fail
to load can ever be written.
Reject on entry every duplicate the saved roster would reject on loading
